subject: zoology_2
question_text: Define vital capacity. What is its significance?

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.47, VSAQ 54. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: Two marks: the definition and the use. Students often write VC = TV + ERV + IRV and stop before the significance.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Breathing and Exchange of Gases · 2 marks

steps.label: Definition
steps.why: Vital capacity measures the largest single breath a person can move, so it must be defined from a forced expiration and not a quiet one.
common_mistakes: Defining it as the total air in the lungs. Residual volume is left out.
Leaving out the word forced. A quiet breath gives a smaller value.
steps.memory_tip: Blow all the way out, then take the biggest breath in.
steps.margin_note: Give the definition, then the sum. Both are marked.
lines: Vital capacity is the maximum volume of air
a person can breathe in after a forced
It includes tidal volume, expiratory reserve

steps.label: Significance
steps.why: A lung that is stiff, blocked or partly destroyed cannot move as much air, so the figure falls before the patient feels much.
common_mistakes: Writing that it measures oxygen in the blood. It measures a volume of air.
Giving no use at all. The second mark is for the use.
steps.memory_tip: A small vital capacity points to a lung disease.
steps.margin_note: One line is enough for the significance.

lines.text: It helps in diagnosing lung diseases
